bull_bear.body: Punjabi market execution risk; festival breakeven delayed beyond FY28; AI regulatory uncertainty; subscription growth slower than expected; content ROI misjudgment on new releases
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, long-term oriented; emphatic on economic rigor (no vanity buys), proud of operational efficiency (Pocket Aces breakeven), bullish on India’s subscription runway, dismissive of AI-generated content threat, focused on institutionalizing IP as infrastructure
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Pocket Aces’ digital muscle is now a cost-saving engine for music marketing, not just a content creator; UN40’s non-music elements (comedy, games) are strategic differentiators reducing artist dependency; Bhansali deal effectively locks in premium Hindi film music without upfront licensing fees; Saregama’s non-digital revenue (physical, radio, sync) remains #1 in India despite digital focus
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend per share has been raised over the cycle: INR 3.0 (FY22), 3.0 (FY23), 4.0 (FY24), 4.5 (FY25), 4.5 (FY26); dividend paid in FY26 was INR 868 Mn.
- The financial-charts slide shows Net Debt to Equity Ratio as NIL; current borrowings are footnoted as 'temporary use of WC limits'.
- Since FY22, INR 7,500 Mn of fresh fund raise through QIP has been added to shareholders' equity.
- Net worth stood at INR 17,547 Mn as at 30-Jun-26 versus INR 16,927 Mn as at 31-Mar-26; the company also holds investments in bank FDs (maturity over 3 months) and mutual funds of INR 2,030 Mn (FY26: INR 1,889 Mn) outside reported cash.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest music IP library in India - 1,80,000+ songs across 14+ languages, plus 70+ films, 55+ digital series and over 10k+ hours of television serials
- Very long-duration IP economics: new content is structured to pay back in approximately five years, fully amortise over roughly a decade, and continue earning at near-90% margins for 60-80 years thereafter
- Owned distribution reach - YouTube channels generating 1,123 Bn+ views and 200 Mn+ subscribers
- Monetisation diversified across six revenue streams, reducing dependence on any single distribution channel or vertical
- Breadth of platform relationships - 50+ music licensing platforms, 30+ streaming platforms, 20+ broadcasting platforms and 8+ social media platforms
- Agreement with Bhansali Productions secures premium Hindi film music on pre-agreed commercial terms, insulating the Company from competitive bidding
- Artiste management roster of 300+ artistes with a combined digital footprint of 410 Mn+, enabling cross-monetisation across Music, Video and Live Events
- Disciplined pre-licensing model in digital series - projects greenlit only after securing platform interest and approval
- Proprietary analytics and AI-led production tooling that cut music-video production from over two weeks to a few days
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Infringement of the Company's intellectual property / piracy — The core business relies on monetising music, film and content rights, so unauthorised use or piracy directly impacts revenue, weakens the value of exclusive content and increases legal costs, while damaging credibility as a rights holder and making licensing harder to enforce. Flagged as a material issue with negative financial implications; mitigated by a dedicated monitoring team and membership of industry body IMI (Indian Music Industry).
- Investment return risk on content and artiste spend — Investments in content and artiste collaborations may not always deliver expected returns, affecting profitability and future growth. Mitigated by diversified, data-driven investments across music, films, digital content and events, a focus on low-risk high-return projects, retained IP ownership, and piloting initiatives before scaling.
- Licensing renewal and rate risk — Unfavourable licensing renewals or rates may reduce revenue streams. Mitigated by a large, high-quality content library with multiple platform deals to reduce dependence on any one counterparty, and pre-licensing contracts that secure upfront revenue.
- Content cost inflation and competitive intensity — Increased competition may drive up content costs or lower success rates, impacting overall performance. Mitigated through industry relationships, a diversified multilingual content strategy, predictive analytics and partnerships with established artistes.
- Digital disruption and shifting consumption habits — Rapid technology evolution and changing consumption habits may impact traditional revenues; digitalisation has already altered how music revenue is generated. The Company invests in digital innovation, new platforms and tech upgrades, and uses data analytics to drive content strategy - treating digitalisation as an opportunity as well as a risk.
- Content and platform concentration — Over-reliance on certain genres or platforms can limit reach and revenue. Mitigated by a broad portfolio spanning multiple languages, genres, formats and platforms.
- Talent attraction and retention (human risk) — Difficulty attracting and retaining talent can reduce operational efficiency in a business whose output depends on creative and monetisation expertise. Mitigated by a balanced scorecard for performance, employee stock options, decentralisation and regular engagement and training programmes.
- Regulatory change, including environmental compliance in the products business — Changes in regulations or IP infringement may harm business operations and financial outcomes; separately, the products business must comply with E-waste and Plastic waste regulations, where non-adherence to changing environmental legislation on generation, collection and disposal can create monetary risk. Mitigated by proactive legal monitoring, industry engagement, robust anti-piracy efforts and close collaboration with relevant authorities.
- Macro-economic weakness and inflation compressing discretionary spend — A weak macroeconomic environment combined with high inflation may reduce the disposable income of the target market for discretionary entertainment spend. Management's counter-argument is that rising per capita income, increasing digitisation and greater affordability position the Indian economy to drive M&E growth and subscriber penetration.
- Funding availability for content and artiste development (finance risk) — Limited cash or financing could restrict investment in content and artiste development. Mitigated by maintaining net debt-free status and strong operating cash flows to ensure sufficient liquidity.

FY25 one-off Diljit tour), UN40 festival loss in Q4 due to inaugural spend; Video: INR 108cr (-44% YoY) due to deliberate wind-down of Yoodlee film production; Artist management: 300+ artists, 400M+ digital followers; Retail (Carvaan): Stable, integrated with live events; Bhansali: Strategic minority stake, exclusive access to future film music via performance-linked valuation
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Stated strategy on the cover slide: 'OWN THE IP IN PERPETUITY. THEN COMPOUND IT ACROSS EVERY FORMAT THAT INDIA'S DIGITAL BOOM OPENS UP.'
- Two moats claimed: an owned catalogue of 1,80,000+ songs (master and underlying works, in perpetuity, global territory) and a large owned audience of 680 Mn+ subscribers and followers across the portfolio.
- Owned content beyond music: 70+ films, 55+ digital series, 10K+ hours of TV, across 14+ Indian languages.
- Deck frames revenue as 'Diversified Across Segments, Partners and Revenue Sources - No Single Point of Dependence', spanning platform (Spotify, YouTube, Netflix, JioHotstar, Sun TV, Doordarshan, Instagram), brand (Myntra, Indriya, Unilever, KFC, Hero) and customer (Amazon, Vijay Sales, BookMyShow, District, PVR).
- The company describes an 'Entertainment Flywheel framework' in which the integrated ecosystem across music, video, live events and artiste management maximises the value of its intellectual property.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group] Saregama is part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka (RPSG) Group, whose businesses span power and energy, carbon black, retail, IT enabled services, FMCG, media and entertainment, and agriculture.
- [Demerger] FY23 numbers are re-stated, as applicable, post the impact of the demerger; the FY26 cash flow also shows INR 36 Mn 'Transferred pursuant to Demerger/ Finnet'.
- [Base effect] Live events is described as lumpy in nature, with FY25 carrying a one-off Diljit Dosanjh India tour - the reason FY26 headline revenue (INR 9,846 Mn) is below FY25 (INR 11,713 Mn) while the deck flags revenue up excluding the one-off live-events base.
- [Regulation] An exceptional item of INR (85) Mn in FY26 is attributed to the impact of the new labour code.
- [Non-GAAP] The disclaimer states EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, PAT Margin, Debt to Equity, and ROE are non-GAAP measures not defined under Ind AS and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Saregama owns, acquires and creates music and entertainment intellectual property and monetises it across multiple channels. The Music segment - Licensing, Artiste Management and Retail - licenses the catalogue to audio and video OTT platforms, broadcasters, social media platforms and brands, manages an artiste roster, and sells consumer music products such as Carvaan and vinyl records. Alongside this, the Company runs a Live Events business of artiste-led concerts and owned-IP festivals, and a Video business of digital series, short-format content and television programming, having stepped back from capital-heavy in-house film production in favour of minority-ownership, IP-led positions.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build an integrated entertainment ecosystem - the Entertainment Flywheel - by reinforcing each vertical and the interconnections between them, rather than scaling individual businesses in isolation
- Three cross-cutting accelerators run across the verticals: AI & Data Analytics, Brand Partnerships and Performance Marketing
- Digital Tailwinds: leverage macro-expansion of internet users, higher per-user consumption and the migration of advertising budgets to digital platforms
- Monetisation Catalysts: capture structural upside from acceleration of paid audio subscriptions and the potential for short-format digital applications to share advertising revenue
- Market Share Expansion: sustain targeted new-content investment to capture and control 25% to 30% of all new music released in India
- Financial Discipline: secure high-value IP and marketing efficiencies through the strategic stake in Bhansali Productions (predictable costs for Hindi film music) and Pocket Aces (in-house digital amplification)
- Maintain a non-negotiable five-year payback requirement on all new music content acquired
- Shift the Video vertical away from capital-heavy in-house film production toward risk-mitigated, IP-led, asset-light formats anchored by significant-minority ownership positions, while retaining ownership of underlying IP wherever feasible
- Run Live Events on two legs - lean, artiste-led concerts using third-party venues with low working capital, and higher-margin owned-IP shows and festivals - under a test-and-scale operating philosophy
- Reorient Carvaan retail toward profitability via e-commerce and modern trade, SKU rationalisation and organisational restructuring, while scaling vinyl
- Refresh the legacy catalogue with licensed Generative AI tools through a dedicated AI efficiency team to make 20th-century content monetisable for Gen Z audiences
- Expand internationally in live entertainment and events through the newly incorporated UAE subsidiary, and pursue selective strategic investments and acquisitions in the creator economy
- Pursue entertainment opportunities on the strength of their IP potential, monetisation and returns rather than the stature of the opportunity alone
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Saregama is an asset-light, IP-led business: its expansion is content-portfolio and corporate-development led rather than plant-and-capacity led, and the AR discloses no manufacturing capacity. The core programme is the commitment to invest INR 10,000 Mn between FY 25 and FY 27 to expand the music IP portfolio, targeting 25-30% of all new Indian music content, with each acquisition governed by a five-year payback framework. During FY 26 the Company acquired NAV Records to build its position in the Haryanvi music ecosystem, and entered an agreement with Bhansali Productions securing premium Hindi film music on pre-agreed commercial terms - a structure the MD describes as taking a 28% to 49.9% stake funded entirely from internal accruals with an initial payment of INR 3,250 Mn. On the corporate-development side, the Company completed the second tranche acquisition in Pocket Aces Pictures Private Limited on 3rd April, 2025 by acquiring 4,111 securities, lifting fully diluted shareholding to 90.93%; Pocket Aces in turn acquired 100% of Finnet Media Private Limited on 19th November, 2025 (with a further 2,88,235 OCPS to be acquired after two years), extending the Group into influencer marketing and creator management. International footprint was extended by incorporating the wholly owned subsidiary Saregama Performing Arts & Music Festivals L.L.C S.O.C in Dubai Mainland, UAE - approved by the Board on 5th September, 2025 with the Commercial Licence issued on 20th February, 2026 - to build live entertainment and events across the Middle East and other global markets. Within the existing verticals, expansion is format-led: adjacent formats such as Carvaan, Vinyl and live experiences, a test-and-scale approach to new live formats including the inaugural proprietary two-day UN40 festival in Bengaluru in March 2026, and a deliberate scaling down of capital-heavy in-house film production in favour of risk-mitigated, IP-led formats with significant-minority ownership positions. Retail expansion runs the other way - Carvaan is being reoriented toward profitability through a shift to e-commerce and modern trade, SKU rationalisation and organisational restructuring, while vinyl volumes scaled from 4,000 units in FY 24 to 27,000 units in FY 26.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian M&E sector expanded 9.1% to INR 2.78 Tn in 2025, outpacing nominal GDP per capita growth of 7.7%; digital media surpassed television to become the largest single segment, breaching the INR 1 Tn milestone
- Global recorded music revenue grew 7% to USD 32 Bn in 2025 with streaming at 69% of revenue, while India remains among the most under-penetrated large music markets globally - a structural opportunity, not a constraint
- India's paid music-subscription penetration of 3% versus 18-67% in comparable markets, with dual levers of subscriber expansion and rising ARPU (emerging-markets label-share ARPU of ~8 USD against ~31 USD in developed markets, a ~4x runway)
- Music subscription penetration remains under 3% despite India housing 18% of the world's population; the transition toward subscription-led consumption is an important long-term opportunity as willingness to pay for premium content rises
- Organised live events grew 44% in 2025 to INR 145 Bn, the fastest-growing M&E vertical, with concerts, ticketed events and IP-led properties driving growth; devotional events benefit from rising engagement in spiritual experiences and government support for pilgrimage and cultural tourism, and comedy is now a top contributor to ticketed revenue
- Video entertainment scaled to a record INR 205 Bn in 2025 with theatrical up 14%, though secondary-window economics continued to rationalise; India's micro-drama market at INR 6.5 Bn is expected to grow over 50% annually through 2028 on Tier-II/Tier-III adoption, low-cost AI-enabled production and UPI AutoPay
- Music IP is a resilient, long-duration asset class with recurring monetisation across audio and video streaming, social media, publishing, licensing, films, television, gaming, live entertainment, consumer products and AI-enabled platforms
- Rising consumption of regional content and the global appeal of Indian music enhance the long-term value of high-quality IP portfolios
- New content economics: pays back in approximately five years, fully amortises over roughly a decade, and continues earning at near-90% margins for 60-80 years thereafter
- With Pocket Aces achieving breakeven during the year, the short-format and digital series business is expected to deliver healthy growth in the years ahead
- Live Events focus is on differentiated formats, a capital-efficient model and improving profitability over time
- The Bhansali Productions partnership secures marquee Hindi film music at predictable costs, insulating the Company from unpredictable competitive bidding wars
- Exclusive, pre-agreed pipeline for marquee Hindi film music secured through the Bhansali Productions partnership, expected to represent approximately 30% to 40% of future Hindi film music acquisitions
- Premium Hindi film music pipeline supporting the Music segment through the partnership with Bhansali Productions, on pre-agreed commercial terms
- Digital series operate on a disciplined pre-licensing model - projects greenlit only after securing platform interest and approval; the FY 26 slate included Bakaiti (ZEE5), High Heels S2 (YouTube), Yeh Saali Naukri (YouTube) and Hunter 2 (Amazon MX Player)
- Television is a stable, capital-efficient vertical generating recurring revenue through commissioned programming on long-standing broadcaster relationships
- Licensing pre-licensing contracts used to secure upfront revenue
- Management cites a strong content pipeline supporting the integrated operating model
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Saregama delivered record EBITDA and PAT driven by music vertical growth post-Airtel Wynk exit, with strategic content spend discipline and new monetization levers like UN40 festival and Bhansali partnership creating durable upside; the shift from vanity-driven acquisitions to 5-year payback discipline and AI efficiency gains positions it as India’s dominant music IP infrastructure play.
